content:
A robot begins at the point `(0, 0)`, the origin, sitting on a 2D plane. After running through a list of its moves, decide whether this robot **finishes at** `(0, 0)`.

You receive a string `moves` describing the move sequence of the robot, where `moves[i]` describes the `ith` move. Permitted moves are `'R'` (right), `'L'` (left), `'U'` (up), and `'D'` (down).

Return `true` _if the robot returns to the origin after it finishes all of its moves, or_ `false` _otherwise_.

**Note**: Which way the robot is "facing " does not matter. `'R'` will always send the robot one step to the right, `'L'` will always send it left, etc. Also, assume each move covers the same step length.

**Example 1:**

**Input:** moves =  "UD "
**Output:** true
**Explanation**: The robot moves up once, and then down once. All moves have the same magnitude, so it ended up at the origin where it started. Therefore, we return true.

**Example 2:**

**Input:** moves =  "LL "
**Output:** false
**Explanation**: The robot moves left twice. It ends up two  "moves " to the left of the origin. We return false because it is not at the origin at the end of its moves.

**Constraints:**

*   `1 <= moves.length <= 2 * 104`
*   `moves` only contains the characters `'U'`, `'D'`, `'L'` and `'R'`.
title: Does Robot Finish At Start Point
